notes: Masculine singular سعيد (sa'id) agrees with the speaker; a female speaker says سعيدة (sa'ida).
Masculine singular متعب (mut'ab); feminine متعبة (mut'aba). Unvocalized متعب could also be read mut'ib ('tiring'); both readings are masculine, so the gender verdict is unaffected.
Masculine singular passive participle مشغول (mashghul) agrees with the speaker; feminine مشغولة (mashghula).
Masculine singular participle متأكد (muta'akkid) agrees with the speaker; feminine متأكدة (muta'akkida).
Feminine singular سعيدة (sa'ida) agrees with the speaker; a male speaker says سعيد (sa'id).
Feminine singular passive participle مشغولة (mashghula); masculine مشغول (mashghul).
Feminine singular participle متأكدة (muta'akkida); masculine متأكد (muta'akkid).
The 1st-person singular imperfect prefix أ- in أدرس (adrusu) is identical for male and female speakers; Arabic first-person verb forms carry no speaker-gender information.
Masculine سعيد agrees with the third-person subject هو (he), not the speaker; the speaker's gender is unknown.
Feminine متعبة agrees with the third-person subject هي (she); no first-person gender marking.
Third-person descriptive nominal sentence; no first-person gender marking.

glossEn: Are you tired? (asked of a woman)
notes: Feminine pronoun أنتِ (anti) and adjective متعبة mark the ADDRESSEE, not the speaker; the speaker's gender is unknown. Kasra written on أنتِ only, to disambiguate from masculine أنتَ (anta); otherwise unvocalized.
Feminine سعيدة agrees with the referent أختي (my sister), not the speaker.
Feminine متعبة inside quoted speech belongs to the quoted speaker (قالت, 'she said'), not the narrator.
